name: Licensed Boundary Calculus Transactions
description: Builds partial licensed morphisms, factorization and quantitative defect profiles. Composed transactions concatenate traces with additive ledgers and no universal semantic composer exists.

program.name: Certificates and Confession
program.summary: A construction method adds comparison data and verifies the original relation; a confession method transforms the problem, omits a coordinate and transports the result through a soundness theorem. The confession routes for the kernel share the canonical dependency-pair rank, the typed external-license schemas are related by quasi-functors with one irreversible license stage, and licensed transactions compose with ledgers while no rule recovers the composite semantic profile from the factor capabilities alone.

oneLine: Partial licensed morphisms compose with five-factor factorization and additive trace ledgers, while semantic profiles require supplied composite data and admit no universal composer.
summary: Licensed boundary calculus studies partial morphisms with explicit domains and admitted edges over abstract rewriting systems with audit scopes. It asks when a morphism is total, how composites fail in domain or edge admission, and how traces and resource counts behave under composition. Every partial morphism equals its domain-edge-quotient-image-inclusion composite, and totality holds for a morphism with a total representative while the partial-chain fixture has none. Finite structural counts add across composites with fiber costs at most multiplying and coverage gaps monotone, and event counting turns trace append into ledger addition respected by every additive valuation. Integrated transactions bundle a morphism with semantics and a trace, so certified composites concatenate traces and add ledgers under a supplied composite capability. Two limits bound this calculus: distinct adequate decorations of one identity composite give different profiles, and one morphism-trace pair carries different semantic profiles.
boundary: Admitted in-domain edges compose and count additively on the licensed side, while out-of-domain states and rejected edges form disjoint additive defects that block totalization and surjectivity. Quotient-image dynamics forward-simulate always but agree with image steps on the lifting side and diverge on the non-lifting side, marked by an image self-step with no quotient edge. Semantic profiles follow the morphism-trace pair on the supplied-capability side and separate from it on the other side, where one identity composite admits two adequate decorations with different costs and one morphism-trace pair carries two profiles, so no factor-only rule recovers all composites.

conclusions.statement: For every partial licensed morphism F, canonicalComposite F equals F.

There is no rule from two raw identity capabilities whose output equals the semantic profile of every adequate composite capability for the raw identity composite, and the original and zero-cost composite capabilities have unequal profiles with minimum repair costs 1 and 0.

There is no extractor from a licensed morphism and event trace to a semantic profile returning the correct profile for every integrated transaction over the chain carrier with Unit semantics, and the two-alternative and orientation transactions have equal morphisms and equal event traces but unequal semantic profiles.
For every partial licensed morphism F, comp (id A) F equals F and comp F (id B) equals F, and for all composable F G H, comp (comp F G) H equals comp F (comp G H).
For any partial licensed morphism F, F.IsTotal holds if and only if there exists a total morphism T with T.toPartial equal to F.

For every composable F and G over finite carriers, undefined counts add with downstream counts and rejected counts add with downstream counts and maximum fiber cardinality of the composite is at most the product of maxima and final coverage gap is monotone.

Given first and second integrated transactions and a composite capability under the same class assumptions, undefined counts add with downstream counts and fiber cardinalities multiply and coverage gaps are monotone and ledgers add.
Given any additive valuation and first and second integrated transactions with a composite capability, the valuation of the composite ledger equals the sum of the valuations of the factor ledgers.

Given first and second integrated transactions and a certified capability for their composite, the composite event trace equals the first trace appended with the second trace and its ledger equals the first ledger plus the second ledger.
For any morphism F, quotient-image exactness holds if and only if the quotient-to-image map satisfies step lifting from the kernel quotient to the image, with no additional hypotheses.
For a partial morphism F over finite carriers, targetCoverageGap F equals zero if and only if F.map is surjective onto the target carrier.
For all traces first and second, countEvents of first appended with second equals countEvents first plus countEvents second.
For every valuation and all ledgers left and right, evaluation of left plus right equals evaluation of left plus evaluation of right.
There is no total licensed morphism T with T.toPartial equal to partialChain_fixture.
There is no rational value such that both bit and joule policies return some value on the mixed fixture.

openPoints: Finite undefined, edge, fiber and coverage counts and semantic profiles require Fintype carriers, with DecidableEq and Fintype for defect and action types where stated.
Integrated trace, ledger and profile composition laws apply with an explicit composite or certified capability linking semantics to composite admission.
Guarded Hartley and log-ratio values are available under normalization hypotheses with licensed multiplicity at most raw multiplicity.
Default licensed quotient and observation use classical choice for the codomain point.
Vector valuation is unconditional for explicit weights, while scalar exchange rates remain external policy with no common scalar on the mixed fixture and no unique total rate extension.

subTopics.name: Core partial morphisms, restriction and factorization
Execution gates, event semantics and trace adequacy
Licensing data, boundary completion and expiry faces

files.summary: The file defines a boundary-operator record carrying a partial domain, an apply function, gauge data, a channel, payload extraction and cost data together with six proof fields. Its projection theorems restate the six stored laws for any record. It also builds a finite example on Option Bool to Bool with two live inputs collapsing to false and true left without preimage, showing the irreversibility and payload non-recovery laws hold non-vacuously.
files.conclusion: The file records a six-law boundary-operator structure and exhibits a finite two-input instance satisfying all six laws non-vacuously.

files.summary: This file defines two morphism defects for licensed reduction morphisms: state collapse, where distinct source states map to one target state, and edge rejection, where a raw source edge is not admitted. It proves the Bool orientation fixture collapses states but rejects no edge, while the KO7 distinction fixture rejects the diagonal eqW branch but has no state collapse because its map is identity. The conjunction of the four fixture facts gives axis independence of orientation and distinction at the defect level.
files.conclusion: Orientation and distinction are independent morphism defects with opposite collapse and rejection behavior.

files.summary: Defines a typed-refusal runtime status pairing a classifier with its support proof, and an engine contract pairing a boundary operator with an optional status. Provides constructors for an empty contract, for adding a generic classifier with its support proof, and for the canonical TypedOutput package. Proves that an advertised status classifies every output inside the refusal support and that both constructors project to such a status.
files.conclusion: Any contract exposing a typed-refusal status advertises a classifier whose values lie in the refusal support for every input.

files.summary: This file defines licensed quotient data with gauge action and projection plus a factorization certificate requiring B apply to factor through projection. It proves the codomain is nonempty and builds a default Option encoding with identity gauge and True license that yields an unconditional factorization certificate for any operator. A finite toy quotient with Z2 action factors the toy boundary operator through a constant false observation.
files.conclusion: Every boundary operator factors through a licensed quotient via an unconditional default encoding, as illustrated by the toy factorization.

files.summary: This file defines pointwise agreement of two observation maps on the boundary-operator image and proves any two factorizations agree there because both equal B apply. It bundles existence with pointwise agreement into engine-grade and unconditional packages and a universal package quantifying over all certificate pairs. Toy specializations discharge both bundles for the toy operator, with carrier isomorphism explicitly excluded from the scope.
files.conclusion: Any two licensed-quotient factorizations agree pointwise on the boundary image, giving unconditional existence plus universal agreement including for the toy operator.

files.summary: Lifts a usable-rules concrete route candidate into a confession-core witness and route evidence with projection equalities for core, generic route and forgetting rank. Defines a three-point TRS plug with blocked, direct and shadow inputs, a constant TypedOutput verdict, a Z2 gauge swapping the live points, a runtime channel, payload tags and log-cost, assembled as TRS_BoundaryOperator with proofs of partiality, irreversibility, gauge covariance, channel preservation, payload non-recovery and cost bound. Proves the plug is inhabited, satisfies typed-refusal completeness from the generic TypedOutput completeness theorem, and factors through a one-point licensed quotient.
files.conclusion: The TRS plug is an inhabited boundary operator with typed-refusal completeness and licensed-quotient factorization collapsing two live inputs to one verdict with unrecoverable payload.

files.summary: This module enumerates four refusal constructors Y N U H and defines support as the universal set, so every value is trivially supported. It packages arbitrary maps into the carrier as classifiers and defines the canonical TypedOutput to refusal map. It proves constructor coverage and classifier codomain typing with completeness for arbitrary and TypedOutput operators and engine-grade exhaustive versions, noting that semantic correctness and disjointness need further predicates.
files.conclusion: Every classifier lands in universal refusal support and every refusal value is one of four constructors, giving completeness for arbitrary and TypedOutput operators.

files.summary: Defines AdditiveValuation as an explicit map from event kinds to resource vectors and evaluation of finite ledgers by weighted sum. Proves evaluation is additive over ledger addition, evaluates singletons to scalar multiples of weights, and transports trace concatenation to vector addition. Introduces directUnitValuation with unit weights on directly interpretable dimensions and zero elsewhere, and checks it evaluates the refusal-certificate fixture to 1 bit.
files.conclusion: Every explicit vector valuation is unconditionally additive and trace concatenation maps to vector addition.

files.summary: Declares the finite inductive BoundaryEventKind with fourteen event kinds and the structure BoundaryEvent wrapping a kind. Provides edgeRefusal_event_fixture as an inhabited example and proves its kind equals edgeRefusal.
files.conclusion: The finite event vocabulary is inhabited by a concrete refusal event.

files.summary: Defines EventLedger as finitely supported counts and countEvents by recursion using singletonEventLedger. Proves that append and EventTrace.comp map to ledger addition. Evaluates the refusal-certificate fixture to one refusal plus one certificate bit and its edgeRefusal coordinate to 1.
files.conclusion: Counting a concatenated trace equals addition of the two ledgers, exemplified by the refusal-certificate fixture.

files.summary: Defines EventTrace as lists of boundary events and comp as list append. Proves empty and comp unit laws and associativity. Provides the two-event refusal-certificate fixture of length 2.
files.conclusion: Sequential trace composition is associative with empty-trace units, exemplified by the two-event fixture.

files.summary: Defines ResourceKind with eight coordinate labels and ResourceVector as finitely supported natural-valued functions. Provides the bit-joule fixture with one bit and two joules, evaluates both coordinates, and proves bit and joule labels distinct.
files.conclusion: The mixed one-bit two-joule vector evaluates correctly on each coordinate with bit distinct from joule.

files.summary: Defines pointwise resource order, optional scalar policies, monotonicity and nonzeroness, with bit-only and joule-only policies. Proves both policies monotone and nonzero on the mixed fixture. Proves they disagree with values 1 versus 2 and that no rational value is returned by both on that fixture.
files.conclusion: Two monotone nonzero scalar policies disagree on the mixed fixture so no common scalar value exists for both.

files.summary: Defines pointwise relation and predicate inclusion, one-step preservation, and SafeRel as the largest subrelation of R that cannot cross from P to not-P. Proves SafeRel preserves P, is greatest among such subrelations, deletes exactly boundary-crossing edges, and mutually stabilizes with the persistent Box license. Places actual relation-predicate pairs in a partial order with two stable endpoints and exhibits a safe-failed fixture where those endpoints are incomparable.
files.conclusion: Two universal repairs fix each other exactly yet separate into incomparable stable endpoints on a real fixture.

files.summary: Defines boundary isomorphisms preserving restricted dynamics and shows they transport finite paths and induce equivalences of path-constant observables. Defines finite release data and pushforward ensemble laws and proves a coupled boundary-mass-release isomorphism determines the law. Exhibits a two-state static Boolean countermodel with identity boundary and release but swapped mass giving different laws, so uncoupled determination fails.
files.conclusion: Coupled boundary-mass-release transport determines the released ensemble law, but separately chosen isomorphisms admit a finite countermodel with different laws.

files.summary: Defines the boundary predicate Bd as greatest forward-stable sublicense with its carrier and restricted dynamics, plus step-lifting morphisms. Proves forward transport under lifting plus license preservation and reflection via simulation, with functor laws for identities and composition. Instantiates the same object in four fibers: KO7 persistent distinction, compact-uniform metric separation, empty role boundary, and empty DP boundary with licensed issue.
files.conclusion: The persistent boundary is functorial on lifting preserving morphisms and has the KO7 comparator, metric separation, role and DP channels as four exact fibers.

files.summary: Constructs channel collapse dynamics on Bool times Bool and proves diagonal states are echoes while off-diagonal states are exogenous. Packages these as channelExpiry with licensed issue and unlicensed consume whose expiry discharges through license_expiry_iff_reachable_echo. Proves transport to equality and quote expiry is empty by consume self-loop obstructions and constructs an inhabited morphism into role expiry.
files.conclusion: Channel endogenization is a fourth live expiry object that cannot map to equality or quote expiry but maps into role erasure.

files.summary: Defines admittedEdgeARS restricting the carrier to the domain subtype with the admitted relation, plus edgeRestrictionOnDomain and admittedStateMap morphisms. Proves admitted membership equals the original admitted relation and the residual map equals the original map. Proves the pure edge-rejection fixture admits no edge.
files.conclusion: Edge restriction keeps exactly the admitted source edges with unchanged state map, and pure rejection admits nothing.

files.summary: Builds domain-edge, kernel and image composites and the full five-factor canonicalComposite for every partial licensed morphism. Proves the composite preserves domain and admitted edges and equals the original morphism universally and unconditionally. Packages the CanonicalBoundaryFactorization certificate with canonicalFactorization and checks orientation and distinction fixtures as instances.
files.conclusion: Every partial licensed morphism equals its five-factor domain-edge-quotient-image-inclusion composite.

files.summary: Defines the DomainCarrier subtype and domainRestrictedARS with raw steps restricted to the domain, plus the canonical domainRestriction partial morphism. Proves domain equivalence, map equality, and nonempty carrier iff the domain is inhabited. Checks the partial-chain fixture maps source to itself.
files.conclusion: Domain restriction isolates exactly the defined states with identical domain and map, nonempty exactly when defined somewhere.

files.summary: Defines ImageCarrier as the range of the state map and imageARS with target steps restricted to the range, plus imageMap and imageInclusion morphisms. Proves value formulas, inclusion after map equals the original map, and surjectivity onto the image. Shows pure state collapse identifies two domain points in the image.
files.conclusion: The state map factors through its range surjectively with inclusion recovering the original map, identifying collapsed states.

files.summary: Defines KernelQuotient by the observer kernel, kernelProjection, kernelQuotientARS with existential direct-image steps, and the projection morphism. Proves projection equality iff map values agree, surjectivity, and unique factorization for maps constant on fibers. Shows pure state collapse identifies source and target classes.
files.conclusion: The kernel quotient identifies exactly fiber-equal states with surjective projection and unique factorization of fiber-constant maps.

files.summary: Defines identity and sequential composition for partial licensed morphisms with domain and admission formulas. Proves left and right unit laws and associativity with explicit domain, admission and map equations. Provides pure rejection, collapse and combined fixtures and proves collapse is not step-reflecting and identity composes with the partial fixture.
files.conclusion: Partial licensed morphisms form an associative unital composition algebra where forward simulation need not reflect steps.

files.summary: Defines PartialLicensedReductionMorphism with domain, admitted subrelation, endpoint conditions, partial map and simulation, plus total embedding toPartial and admittedSystem. Proves extensionality equality and multi-step and reachability transport. Provides the partial-chain fixture with source-only domain undefined at target and a total-domain fixture for the chain morphism.
files.conclusion: Partial morphisms lift paths and reachability through the admitted relation with a genuinely partial example.

files.summary: Defines the quotientToImage lift from kernel classes to the image range and proves projection compatibility, injectivity and surjectivity, packaging the carrier equivalence quotientImageEquiv and a forward simulation morphism. Proves the equivalence and morphism share the forward map. Proves the partial-chain image inclusion is not surjective onto the ambient target.
files.conclusion: Kernel quotient and image are equivalent carriers with forward simulation, while image inclusion need not be surjective.

files.summary: Defines domain and edge restrictions with true, composition, idempotence and commutation laws, plus the totality predicate IsTotal, totalization toTotal and round-trip. Proves the exact criterion that IsTotal holds iff a total morphism with equal toPartial exists. Shows the partial-chain fixture admits no total representative.
files.conclusion: State and edge restrictions are commuting idempotent operations with totality exactly when a total representative exists.

files.summary: Reads the KO7 branch transaction as an edge-filter morphism with raw Step and guarded SafeStep systems and identity state map. Proves the state map injective and exhibits the eqW diagonal breaker fixture with a raw edge refused by the guard. The file also contains #check and #print axioms checks of the morphism and fixture claims.
files.conclusion: The distinction face is a licensed morphism whose identity map filters out a genuine raw diagonal edge.

files.summary: Defines PropositionEvidence, three BoundaryDecisions, inputs with domain and admission evidence, the inspect constructor, decisionTrace, DecisionCertificate and the execute gate. Proves commit occurs iff in-domain and admitted, with soundness for state and edge refusals, correct commit outputs and decision-determined traces. Provides state, edge and commit fixtures covering all three decisions.
files.conclusion: The gate commits exactly on admitted in-domain edges with certified refusals and outputs otherwise.

files.summary: Defines the EventSemantics predicate for decision-kind pairs emitted by decisionTrace. Proves membership in decisionTrace holds iff the semantics holds by finite case analysis. Proves certificateBit and reliableRecordBit never satisfy generic semantics.
files.conclusion: Trace membership coincides with event semantics while certificate bits are never generic.

files.summary: Defines the execution ledger as countEvents of the result trace. Proves the ledger equals the count of the trace and of the decision trace, and that composing execution traces preserves append and maps to ledger addition. Checks three fixtures have unit counts for refusal, edge-refusal and replayStep.
files.conclusion: Execution ledgers compose additively over appended decision traces with unit counts on fixtures.

files.summary: Defines DecisionMatchesMorphism, OutputMatchesMorphism and TraceAdequacy with exactness, soundness, completeness and morphism and output agreement. Proves certificates entail decision and output match and execute is always adequate. Provides empty-trace and fabricated certificate-bit counterexamples failing adequacy and proves commit impossible outside the domain.
files.conclusion: Generic execution is always adequate while empty and fabricated certificate traces are inadequate.

files.summary: Defines exact one-step boundary crossings, proof-relevant finite paths with safe-prefix predicates, and failure objects recording first crossing plus decomposition. Proves constructively that an explicit failed path has a first crossing under decidable P and that any failure object refutes Box persistence. Proves classically that global Box failure is equivalent to reachable failing endpoints and to existence of exact failure objects, with safe-failed and always-true fixtures showing necessity and non-vacuity.
files.conclusion: Global Box failure at a licensed source is classically equivalent to existence of an exact first-crossing failure object.

files.summary: The file defines IntegratedBoundaryTransaction, a wrapper that holds only a BoundaryConstructionData record for finite carriers and typed defects and actions. It provides a builder that takes no separate profile or ledger and projections for the licensed morphism, semantic data, event trace, structural profile, semantic profile and event ledger. It proves the semantic scope relation coincides with the morphism admitted relation and that all three quantitative outputs equal the values derived from the single construction datum.
files.conclusion: All quantitative outputs of an integrated transaction equal the values derived from its single construction datum.

files.summary: The file supplies canonical orientation-chain and KO7 distinction transactions through the construction-data builder, so their profiles and ledgers are computed projections. It proves confluence and terminal multiplicity one for the orientation scope and exactness of both semantic profiles. It proves the corresponding event-ledger counts and bundles both faces as nonvacuous inhabitants of the integrated API.
files.conclusion: Both the orientation chain and the KO7 distinction cone occur as integrated transactions with exactly computed semantic profiles and event ledgers.

files.summary: The file defines certified construction data holding a morphism, semantic data, a semantic adequacy certificate and one typed execution input, plus a wrapper whose execution result, trace, ledger and profiles are computed from those fields. It proves the semantic relation equals the admitted relation, that every such transaction has adequate execution and that its ledger is the counted trace. It instantiates a concrete KO7 edge-refusal fixture with refusal decision, unit refusal ledger count and exact semantic profile.
files.conclusion: Every certified integrated transaction has adequate execution and a trace-counted ledger, instantiated by a KO7 refusal fixture with exact profile.

files.summary: The file defines certified semantic capabilities and certified composition whose semantic profile comes from a supplied adequacy certificate for the exact composite relation. It proves left and right identity, associativity, trace concatenation, ledger addition and no scope widening or trust upgrade for the structural backbone. It transports adequacy across pure repair-cost recalibration and uses original versus zero-cost KO7 decorations to prove no factor-only rule can equal every adequate composite profile.
files.conclusion: No universal semantic composer from factor decorations alone exists for the KO7 identity composite.

files.summary: The file defines composite semantic capability as semantic data plus an equivalence to the composite admitted relation. It defines composition of integrated records by composing morphisms, keeping the supplied semantics and appending event traces. It proves the morphism, trace, ledger-addition, derived-profile and associativity laws for this backbone.
files.conclusion: Composed integrated transactions concatenate traces, add ledgers and derive their semantic profile from the supplied composite capability.

files.summary: The file defines BoundaryConstructionData as a package of a partial licensed morphism, semantic construction data, a pointwise equivalence between the semantic scope relation and the admitted relation, and an event trace. It proves a projection theorem that exposes the stored pointwise equivalence for any pair of states.
files.conclusion: The stored pointwise equivalence projects to an equivalence between the semantic scope relation and the admitted relation.

files.summary: The file defines the identity integrated transaction from supplied semantic data whose scope relation matches the system step relation, using the identity morphism and an empty event list. It proves the resulting morphism equals the identity morphism, the trace is empty and the ledger is zero.
files.conclusion: The identity integrated transaction has the identity morphism, empty trace and zero ledger.

files.summary: The file proves quantitative laws for integrated composition that carries an explicit composite capability. It combines domain and edge decompositions, finite fiber and coverage bounds and ledger addition in a universal theorem, with exact pointwise defect formulas. It shows every additive valuation respects such compositions through ledger addition.
files.conclusion: Integrated composition preserves exact structural decompositions, pointwise defect characterizations and additive resource valuations with ledger addition.

files.summary: The file builds a two-alternative variant of the orientation transaction with the same identity morphism and event trace but different certificate data. It proves the two derived semantic profiles differ in their fixed-length certificate floor. It concludes that no extractor from only morphism and trace can recover every semantic profile on the fixed finite chain.
files.conclusion: No morphism-and-trace-only extractor can recover the semantic profile of every integrated transaction.

files.summary: Defines license-expiry objects with distinguished issue and consume states and morphisms preserving dynamics, license and distinguished states. Proves identity, composition and category laws. Supplies three live instances from KO7 development: coalescing equality guard, quote-evaluation peak, and role erasure, each non-vacuous at issue and unlicensed at consume.
files.conclusion: Expiry objects and their morphisms form a category with three live non-vacuous instances.

files.summary: Decides all six ordered transports between equality-coalescence, quote-evaluation and role-erasure expiry: five directions are empty by concrete dynamics or license preservation laws. Constructs the sixth direction from equality to quote through a well-founded guarded rank and canonical merge chain. Adds closure and consumption refinement with canonical full objects and shows the complete table survives that refinement.
files.conclusion: Exactly one of six expiry transports exists, and the five obstructions plus one construction survive closure refinement.

files.summary: Defines audit scopes for location, closure, admission and layer and abstract reduction systems carrying such scopes. Defines length-indexed paths with concatenation and simulation mapping, plus reachability with reflexivity and transitivity. Supplies a two-state one-edge fixture and checks its axioms with #check and #print axioms.
files.conclusion: Finite licensed paths concatenate, map under simulation, and yield transitive reachability with a one-edge fixture.

files.summary: Refines expiry objects with an unlicensed self-obstruction site and repaired dynamics licensed at source, with morphisms preserving both. Proves category laws for ascent morphisms. Forgets each object to a six-step ascent profile with reflection family and proves every object realizes its profile hence is compatible with the dependency-pair profile.
files.conclusion: Every licensed-ascent object realizes its six-step profile and is compatible with the dependency-pair profile.

files.summary: Builds three live licensed-ascent objects over equality, role and quote expiry with explicit obstructions and repairs. Lifts the five expiry obstructions to empty ascent hom-sets and lifts equality-to-quote to an ascent morphism. Proves the full six-way table, its failing laws, and the identity split: distinction and orientation share a comparison witness at profile level but separate with no morphisms at witness level.
files.conclusion: Identical six-step profiles separate at witness level with five blocked directions and one distinction-to-quotation morphism.

files.summary: Defines licensed reduction morphisms combining a proved admitted subrelation with a state map simulating admitted edges. Exposes the admitted guarded system and proves admitted paths map to same-length target paths and reachability lifts. Proves extensional equality and supplies an identity chain fixture with #check and #print axioms verification.
files.conclusion: One-step licensed simulation lifts to same-length paths and reflexive-transitive reachability.

files.summary: Proves that replacing one-step dynamics by reflexive-transitive closure preserves Box licenses, forward invariance, persistent diagonal grade D1p and represented grade D2At. Defines datum completion with idempotence and an identity licensing morphism into the completion. Instantiates the rule on natural-number shift where closure is order and compact-uniform separation and metric licenses become exact Box statements.
files.conclusion: Box, forward invariance, D1p, D2At and metric licenses all survive completion exactly with shift and metric instances.

files.summary: Defines licensing data with carrier, dynamics, license, policy language and consume operation, plus morphisms with state, policy and output maps and explicit preservation-reflection capability tags. Defines capability intersection and identity for composition without guessing mixed capabilities. Proves the package satisfies identity and associativity category laws, strengthened in 2026-08-20 to include associativity.
files.conclusion: Licensing data with capability-intersecting composition satisfy identity and associativity category laws.

files.summary: Defines asynchronous product dynamics and proves its reflexive-transitive closure is exactly componentwise reachability with lifting and projection lemmas. Proves persistent Box licenses compose and decompose componentwise over products. Exposes the existing role-collapse noninjective-discriminator theorem as the typed quotient obstruction and recovers Box over pair lift as D1p, with #check and #print axioms verification.
files.conclusion: Asynchronous product closure and Box licenses compute componentwise, with role erasure as typed quotient obstruction.

files.summary: Exposes the analytic dynamic grade D1u as the metric persistent license without reproving it. States its exact computation rule as compact-uniform separation, the negative rule that pointwise nonvanishing guard-expiry fails the license, and the transport rule that licensed local-uniform convergence passes to reciprocals. Includes #check and #print axioms checks.
files.conclusion: The metric persistent license is exactly compact-uniform separation and transports reciprocal convergence.

files.summary: The file defines one-step post of a set and studies its commutation with direct-image abstraction. It proves forward simulation gives sound inclusion and that equality for every source set is equivalent to step lifting, with the same criterion for the canonical quotient-to-image map versus quotient-image exactness. It gives a finite fixture where abstract-post equality fails and a control where the quotient map is exact while the underlying observation fails pointwise lifting.
files.conclusion: Abstract-post equality for every set holds exactly when the observation satisfies step lifting, and the canonical quotient-to-image map can satisfy this exactness even when the underlying observation does not.

files.summary: The file defines direct-image abstraction alpha and inverse-image concretization gamma for an arbitrary function. It proves their inclusion adjunction with its two one-sided inclusions and characterizes lossless round-trips by injectivity and surjectivity. It proves that disjointness from a target set pulls back along the observation and that equivalence of avoidance for every target set holds exactly when the source image equals the claimed set.
files.conclusion: Direct and inverse image form an adjunction whose round-trips are lossless exactly for injective or surjective maps and whose avoidance transfer is exact exactly when the image equals the claimed set.

files.summary: Defines the root RDRS relation and source and projected abstract rewriting systems, and packages a static projection transaction as an OrientationFace. Proves the transaction projection induces a licensed reduction morphism that admits every source root edge. Provides a Bool-to-Unit fixture where the projection collapses false and true to one point.
files.conclusion: A Bool-to-Unit orientation fixture admits all source edges but collapses distinct source states false and true to one projected state.

files.summary: Defines capability roles, verdicts, exact forward requests, derived provenance and the constructor-closed ProofCarryingLicense family for authorization versus refusal. Proves sound admission from SafeRel and Box evidence, sound refusal from boundary evidence, output-index confinement and type-level exclusion of recovery certificates. Provides accepted and rejected fixtures showing one request is authorizable while the distinct rejected request from the same source is not.
files.conclusion: A genuine boundary-crossing request cannot receive a forward authorization certificate and can only receive a typed refusal.

files.summary: Defines list-prefix, prefix-free binary codes, and an AlternativeCarrier witness package carrying a finite type, a terminal-support equivalence, two count equalities and an injective prefix-free code. Proves that conditional on such a package, each stored count equals the semantic terminal multiplicity. The file supplies no inhabitant of AlternativeCarrier.
files.conclusion: Under a supplied AlternativeCarrier package both stored alternative counts equal the scoped terminal multiplicity.

files.summary: Studies finite target-coverage defects of partial licensed morphisms. Proves the composite image lies in the second-stage image, so composition weakly increases the final-target gap, and gap-zero is equivalent to surjectivity. Exhibits the pure state-collapse fixture as surjective.
files.conclusion: Composite coverage gap dominates the second-stage gap and vanishes exactly for surjective partial maps.

files.summary: Defines actual source-local non-joinable peaks, unoriented peak equality up to branch exchange, and finite defect adequacy as sound, complete and irredundant representation. Proves every represented defect is actual and that an empty certified set forces joinability of immediate peaks. Scope is source-local peaks only.
files.conclusion: An empty certified defect set makes every pair of immediate reducts from the source joinable.

files.summary: Embeds the three-node KO7 local cone into LBC reduction and partial-morphism interfaces without changing relations. Builds raw and licensed semantic scopes and construction data with alternative counts 2 and 1. Proves relation preservation, normalization transport, and that the license rejects the raw difference edge.
files.conclusion: The three-node KO7 cone embeds into LBC interfaces with raw counts 2, licensed counts 1, and an explicitly rejected difference edge.

files.summary: Splits composite domain failure into first-stage failure versus downstream failure after first-stage success. Builds an explicit disjoint equivalence of finite defect types and derives exact additivity of undefined-state counts. Instantiates the law on the partial-chain fixture.
files.conclusion: Composite undefined-state count equals first-stage count plus downstream count after first-stage admission.

files.summary: Gives an exact rejected-edge decomposition for composites: rejection occurs at the first license or downstream on its image, disjointly. Encodes the split as an equivalence of finite types and derives exact additivity of rejected-edge counts. Shows the pure-rejection composite rejects the chain edge.
files.conclusion: Composite rejected-edge count equals first-stage rejected count plus downstream rejected count.

files.summary: Develops finite fiber composition: a dependent-sum equivalence for composite fibers, a pointwise product bound, and a universal maximum-fiber product bound for finite functions. Lifts the bound to partial licensed morphisms via domain inclusions and subtype bounds. Shows the collapse fixture has a genuinely nontrivial fiber.
files.conclusion: Maximum fiber cardinality of a partial composite is at most the product of the two maxima.

files.summary: Defines option-valued rates and Hartley collapse that return none exactly on empty support. Shows two total extensions agree on positive samples yet disagree at zero, so no unique total rate extension exists. Adapts guarded distinction-surface rates and shows the chain fixture collapse is defined.
files.conclusion: There is no unique total rate extension agreeing with ordinary rates on positive samples.

files.summary: Computes all eight semantic-profile coordinates for the fixed three-node raw and licensed fixtures. Shows raw equals multiplicity 2 with defect, cover, cost, rank and floors 1, licensed equals multiplicity 1 with all else 0, and four coordinates drop by exactly one. Equalities apply only to that finite instance.
files.conclusion: Raw and licensed profiles equal the stated exact profiles with a drop of one in four coordinates.

files.summary: Certifies raw and licensed three-node systems with complete adequacy: sound and complete defect vocabularies, repair interpretations preserving the licensed branch, concrete witness carriers at grades 1 and 0, and alternative carriers from terminal supports with explicit prefix-free codes. Shows raw counts two alternatives and licensed counts one.
files.conclusion: Both raw and licensed three-node systems receive complete semantic adequacy certificates with 2 and 1 alternatives respectively.

files.summary: Specializes terminal-support collapse to the finite KO7 cone fixture. Builds the collapse certificate from raw and licensed normalization plus the 1-versus-2 multiplicity bound. Deduces the Hartley log ratio is defined and the collapse value nonnegative.
files.conclusion: The KO7 cone yields a collapse certificate with defined log ratio and nonnegative value.

files.summary: Splits every excluded raw edge into endpoint-domain failure versus in-domain license refusal with disjointness and exact count additivity. Gives a matching upstream-versus-downstream composition law for in-domain refusals and a five-coordinate orthogonal profile. The two fixtures realize opposite 0-versus-1 corners.
files.conclusion: Nonadmitted edges decompose exactly into domain-excluded plus license-rejected counts with a matching in-domain composition law.

files.summary: Defines peak resolution covering both branch removal and joinability of survivors, and repair certificates with protected-relation preservation and sound-complete closes correspondence. Proves closes membership equivalent to resolution, three sufficient resolution conditions, and survival of protected edges.
files.conclusion: For represented defects closes membership is equivalent to peak resolution with protected edges always surviving.

files.summary: Separates computable construction records from proof certificates showing fields denote the actual scoped relation, local defects, repairs, witness language and terminal alternatives. Proves certified multiplicity equals alternative cardinality, defect count equals certified cardinality with actual peaks, and Hartley defined.
files.conclusion: Certified profiles have terminal multiplicity equal to alternative cardinality with every counted defect actual and Hartley defined.

files.summary: Defines construction data with caller-supplied costs and alternative counts and the eight-coordinate profile builder combining scoped, defect, repair, witness and coding quantities. Proves definitional unfolding, a fixed-length lower bound for injective encodings, Hartley definedness under normalization, and zero cover and cost for empty defects.
files.conclusion: The profile builder unfolds definitionally and its fixed-length floor lower-bounds every injective binary encoding of the stated size.

files.summary: Defines scopes storing relation, source and audit, normalization, language and grade metadata with no coherence laws, plus raw and licensed constructors. Defines terminal support, multiplicity and option-valued Hartley with none exactly on empty support. Shows normalization makes Hartley defined and exhibits the normalizing chain fixture.
files.conclusion: Local normalization makes the guarded Hartley coordinate defined and equal to terminal-support entropy.

files.summary: Conjoins four imported finite composition laws for every composable pair of partial licensed morphisms. States both the universal quantitative conjunction and the combined pointwise-plus-quantitative form. Notes the result is a four-law profile, not a complete invariant.
files.conclusion: Every composable pair jointly satisfies the four finite structural composition laws.

files.summary: Defines intrinsic finite counts for domains, raw, admitted and rejected edges, fibers, excess, image and coverage gap, and the eight-coordinate structural profile builder. Proves admission, fiber and image bounds, definitional unfolding, and that exhibited out-of-domain states force positive undefined counts, with the partial chain as fixture.
files.conclusion: Every structural profile lists the intrinsically computed finite defect, fiber and coverage quantities.

files.summary: Defines a terminal-support-collapse certificate conditional on both normalizations and a licensed-at-most-raw multiplicity bound. Projects its real log-ratio value and proves the guarded ratio is some value and the value nonnegative. Theorems only apply those stored hypotheses.
files.conclusion: Every collapse certificate has its log ratio defined as some value and that value nonnegative.

files.summary: Derives least witness grades from carriers of concrete witnesses with upward-closed adequacy. Certifies semantic models only when stored adequacy matches carrier-derived adequacy and scope records kind and least grade. Proves scope grade adequate and lower grades inadequate.
files.conclusion: The scope grade is adequate and all lower grades are inadequate in the certified witness language.

files.summary: Builds a one-step fixture from the empty policy to the raw recD seed or its confluence repair, with confluence as the license predicate. Shows the empty and repaired policies are confluent while the raw seed is not, yielding a safe repaired request with forward license and a raw boundary request with refusal. Treats recovery as an external history token and proves the repaired record has two histories, no global left inverse exists, and neither direction upgrades the other capability.
files.conclusion: Confluence repair has no global deterministic left inverse, recovery evidence cannot manufacture forward admission, and forward admission cannot reconstruct history.

files.summary: Replaces scalar repair rankings with Pareto comparison over retained domain, admitted dynamics, observer factorization and license implication, proving reflexivity, transitivity and preorder structure. Exhibits two Bool profiles that are incomparable with a named failing coordinate in each direction, and shows Box is the greatest forward-invariant predicate repair. Proves the live positional repair compiler is monotone, functorial, confluent, minimal among confluent extensions and idempotent.
files.conclusion: The live repair compiler is monotone, functorial, confluent, minimal and idempotent, while the semantic Pareto order remains partial with an explicit incomparable pair.

files.summary: This file defines exactness of the quotient-to-image dynamics as preservation and reflection of the one-step relation. It proves this exactness is equivalent to step lifting of the canonical quotient-to-image map and equivalent to bisimulation on the image. Under exactness it constructs an abstract rewriting system isomorphism between the kernel quotient and the image. It also proves a finite fixture falsifies exactness, showing the lifting condition cannot be dropped.
files.conclusion: Quotient-to-image dynamics are exact exactly when every image step lifts, in which case the quotient and image are ARS-isomorphic, and the lifting condition cannot be dropped.

files.summary: This file defines forward step and reachability simulation, step and reachability reflection, step lifting, terminality and terminal exactness, plus bisimulation on the image, reduction equivalence, and ARS isomorphism. It proves forward step simulation implies forward reachability simulation and bisimulation on the image implies terminal exactness. It also proves every ARS isomorphism yields forward simulation, lifting, bisimulation, reachability preservation and reflection, reduction equivalence, and terminal exactness.
files.conclusion: Every ARS isomorphism provides forward simulation, step lifting, bisimulation on the image, forward and reflected reachability, reduction equivalence, and terminal exactness.

files.summary: The file builds licensed rank, projective-emitter, coherent, semantic-kernel, generator-preserving, conservation and stage-indexed transaction layers over duplicating systems and reads each as a projection transaction with dimension, license and forgetting boundary. It proves that on constructor-generated schemas, and on the free primitive duplicator, stage-indexed families with invariant licenses and with invariant projection, invariant dimension or a semantic-kernel completion induce static projection families, including canonical-trace, terminal and shadow staticity. It also constructs free instances realizing the computation-to-confession bridge and counterexamples showing that license invariance alone does not imply ambient staticity and that raw emitters need not admit semantic-kernel completions on arbitrary carriers.
files.conclusion: On constructor-generated carriers with invariant licenses, each packaged transaction layer induces a static projection-transaction family, while raw projective data alone and raw faithful data on arbitrary carriers do not force ambient staticity or completion.

files.summary: This file extracts the five tagged typed-output forms with string payloads and a boolean syntactic discipline check for empty fields and license flags. It proves a well-formed licensed T4 abstention is not a violation and an empty T4 refusal is a violation. It ends with axiom-print commands and depends on core Lean only.
files.conclusion: A well-formed licensed T4 abstention passes the discipline check while an empty untyped T4 refusal always violates it.

files.summary: This file checks licensed-quotient factorization for boundary operators. It verifies existence of factoring quotients and pointwise agreement of certificates for the toy operator on Option Bool. It also verifies unconditional existence, uniqueness and universality for arbitrary operators.
files.conclusion: Every boundary operator factors through a licensed quotient with pointwise-unique observables, as instantiated on the toy operator.

files.summary: This file checks licensed-quotient structure for boundary operators. It lists the quotient, certificate and existence declarations and the toy quotient and factorization. It verifies the toy certificate and the existential factorization for the toy operator and from the unconditional theorem.
files.conclusion: The toy boundary operator factors through a licensed quotient, and every operator does.

files.summary: This file checks the toy boundary operator and channel used to illustrate partiality and isolation. It verifies domain membership at some false and some true, non-membership at none, channel behaviour sending some true to some false, and application returning false under a domain hypothesis.
files.conclusion: The toy boundary operator is partial with exactly two live inputs and drops payload as specified.

files.summary: This file checks the TRS instance of the boundary operator. It lists TRS payload tags, inputs, verdicts, gauge actions, channels and the licensed quotient. It verifies liveness on direct and shadow, deadness on blocked, inhabitation, typed refusal completeness and licensed-quotient factorization.
files.conclusion: The TRS operator is inhabited, live on direct and shadow, blocked on blocked, with full refusal completeness and licensed-quotient factorization.

files.summary: This file checks typed refusal completeness for boundary operators. It lists refusal types, support, classifiers and completeness statements for typed outputs. It verifies the classifier on abstention and impossibility outputs, exhaustiveness over four refusal types, and engine-grade completeness.
files.conclusion: Every typed-output boundary operator is refusal-complete over the four refusal types.

claims.reason: Monotonicity and idempotence are stated separately, and many-to-one is shown by distinct histories with equal repairs and by absence of a global left inverse. No single declaration combines all three properties.
